title: Withdrawals failing
summary: Withdrawals began failing around 17:48 UTC on 2026‑10‑15. The strongest hypothesis (HYP‑1, 55 % confidence) is that the external bank‑rails provider degraded or became unreachable, causing the synchronous 4 s HTTPS call from payments‑service to error and the edge‑gateway to return upstream‑502. However, metrics and change‑history back‑ends were unavailable, so the degradation cannot be confirmed and a concurrent config change in payments‑service or edge‑gateway cannot be ruled out. The investigation was stopped because the time budget was reached, leaving the exact root cause unverified.

hypothesis.mechanism: The external bank‑rails provider began returning errors or became unreachable during ~17:45‑18:00 UTC. Payments‑service, which has a hard synchronous HTTPS dependency on bank‑rails with a 4 s timeout (OBS-1), propagates those failures as “bank‑rails call returned an error” (OBS-4). Edge‑gateway then reports upstream‑502 for POST /v1/withdrawals (OBS-2).
predictions: Bank‑rails latency / 5xx‑rate metrics show a sharp rise 17:45‑18:00 UTC.
Change‑history for payments‑service shows no deploy / config‑map / feature‑flag change in the 17:30‑17:45 UTC window.

objections.detail: Bank‑rails latency / 5xx‑rate metrics for 17:45‑18:00 UTC cannot be retrieved (metrics backend down).
Payments‑service change‑history for 17:30‑17:45 UTC cannot be retrieved (change‑history backend down), so we cannot confirm the absence of a config change.

hypothesis.mechanism: A configuration change (e.g., reduced HTTP timeout, altered retry count, switched endpoint URL, or a feature‑flag such as withdrawal‑mode / bank‑rails‑fallback) was rolled out to payments‑service between 17:30‑17:45 UTC. The new, tighter timeout causes previously‑successful bank‑rails calls to be treated as failures, producing the same “bank‑rails call returned an error” logs (OBS-4) and upstream‑502 at the gateway (OBS-2).
predictions: Change‑history for payments‑service shows a deploy / config‑map / feature‑flag update in the 17:30‑17:45 UTC window.
Payments‑service structured logs or a /config endpoint reveal the new, tighter timeout / retry values.

objections.detail: names chg:unknown as the trigger, but no change-history query returned it
The trigger “chg:unknown” is cited but no change‑history query returned a change; the change‑history service is unavailable.
HYP‑1 (bank‑rails degradation) remains a plausible alternative with supporting observations (OBS‑1, OBS‑2, OBS‑4).

hypothesis.mechanism: Edge‑gateway’s per‑route timeout for POST /v1/withdrawals was lowered to less than the payments‑service 4 s bank‑rails client timeout. The gateway aborts the request while payments‑service is still waiting, emitting upstream‑502 (OBS-2). Payments‑service still logs a bank‑rails error because the downstream call eventually fails (OBS-4).
predictions: Edge‑gateway config shows a withdrawal‑route timeout < 4 s after ~17:30 UTC.
Payments‑service latency to bank‑rails stays < 4 s (i.e., no bank‑rails degradation).

objections.detail: names chg:unknown as the trigger, but no change-history query returned it
The trigger “chg:unknown” for an edge‑gateway timeout change is asserted but change‑history queries return no data; the backend is down.
HYP‑1 (bank‑rails degradation) explains the same upstream‑502 and payments‑service error logs without requiring a gateway config change.

hypothesis.mechanism: Transient saturation of the payments database (connection‑pool exhaustion, autovacuum spike, replication lag) caused payments‑service to abort the withdrawal flow before or while calling bank‑rails, resulting in a generic error that is logged as a bank‑rails failure.
predictions: Postgres‑payments metrics show connection‑pool saturation or query‑duration spikes coincident with 17:48‑18:00 UTC.
Payments‑service logs contain DB‑error messages (e.g., pool exhausted) – none observed.

objections.detail: OBS‑4 shows explicit bank‑rails errors from payments‑service, contradicting a postgres‑exhaustion cause.

facts.statement: payments-service has a hard, synchronous HTTPS dependency on the external bank-rails provider with a 4000 ms timeout.
edge‑gateway logged 31 upstream‑502 warnings for POST /v1/withdrawals between 17:48:34 and 17:59:57 UTC.
payments‑service recorded 44 ERROR lines “withdrawal <id> failed: bank‑rails call returned an error” from 17:48:12 to 17:59:37 UTC.
payments‑service also emitted 6 generic 502 errors on POST /v1/checkout between 17:48:21 and 17:58:09 UTC.
postgres‑payments logged a single WARN about autovacuum dead tuples at 17:59:09 UTC.

The core withdrawal request path is edge‑gateway → payments‑service → bank‑rails (hard dependency, HTTPS, 4000 ms timeout) and payments‑service → postgres‑payments (hard dependency, SQL, 2000 ms timeout).

assumptions.statement: The autovacuum warning at 17:59:09 UTC is unrelated to the withdrawal path.
assumptions.reason: Warning occurs after the bulk of failures and no DB‑error logs appear on the withdrawal flow.

assumptions.statement: The bank‑rails provider suffered an un‑announced degradation (errors, latency spikes or partial outage) during ≈17:45‑18:00 UTC.
assumptions.reason: No metrics or logs from bank‑rails are available (GAP-5, GAP-6, GAP-13) but the symptom pattern matches a downstream failure.

assumptions.statement: No configuration change was made to the payments‑service → bank‑rails client (timeout, retry, base‑url) in the 30 min before the first error.
assumptions.reason: Change‑history service is down (GAP-1, GAP-3, GAP-19, GAP-20) so we cannot confirm; assumed pending evidence.

assumptions.statement: A configuration change (e.g., reduced HTTP timeout, altered retry count, switched endpoint URL, or a feature‑flag such as withdrawal‑mode / bank‑rails‑fallback) was rolled out to payments‑service between 17:30‑17:45 UTC.
assumptions.reason: Hypothesis requires a trigger; change‑history unavailable (GAP-1, GAP-21, GAP-22). Assumed for hypothesis construction.

assumptions.statement: The change made previously‑successful bank‑rails calls exceed the new timeout, so they are logged as “bank‑rails call returned an error”.
assumptions.reason: Logically follows from a tighter timeout; no direct observation.

assumptions.statement: Edge‑gateway’s per‑route timeout was lowered to < payments‑service’s 4 s bank‑rails timeout, causing the gateway to abort while payments‑service is still waiting.
assumptions.reason: Explains upstream‑502 while downstream still logs error; config not observed (GAP-1, GAP-19).

actions.description: Enable a short‑circuit / fallback path in payments‑service for withdrawals (e.g., queue for retry or return a user‑friendly error) so that bank‑rails outages do not block the whole flow.
actions.rationale: Immediately reduces customer impact while the upstream provider is unstable.

actions.description: Contact the bank‑rails vendor to obtain an incident report for the 17:45‑18:00 UTC window and negotiate SLA improvements or a status‑page webhook.
actions.rationale: Addresses the most likely external degradation (HYP‑1) and prevents recurrence.

actions.description: Add automated health‑checks and alerting on bank‑rails latency / 5xx rate, and configure a circuit‑breaker in payments‑service with a lower timeout and exponential back‑off.
actions.rationale: Detects future degradations early and limits blast radius.

actions.description: When the metrics and change‑history services recover, query bank‑rails latency/5xx metrics for 17:45‑18:00 UTC and payments‑service change‑history for 17:30‑17:45 UTC to confirm or exclude HYP‑1 and HYP‑2.
actions.rationale: Closes the evidence gaps (GAP‑1, GAP‑2, GAP‑5‑GAP‑14) that prevent a definitive conclusion.

actions.description: Verify whether any payments‑service or edge‑gateway config/feature‑flag changes were deployed in the 17:30‑17:45 UTC window once change‑history is available.
actions.rationale: Rules out HYP‑2 and HYP‑4 which remain plausible alternatives.

open_questions: Did the bank‑rails provider experience a latency spike or error‑rate increase between 17:45‑18:00 UTC?
Was there any payments‑service configuration change (timeout, retry, endpoint, feature flag) deployed between 17:30‑17:45 UTC?
Was the edge‑gateway per‑route timeout for POST /v1/withdrawals altered to a value < 4 s during the same window?
What do the bank‑rails internal logs (az‑a shard) show for the period before 17:48 UTC?
Are there any correlated infrastructure events (network, DNS, cert renewal) that could have affected the bank‑rails HTTPS endpoint?
